<p> <a href="https://crates.io/crates/secp256k1-sys"><img alt="Crate Info" src="https://img.shields.io/crates/v/secp256k1-sys.svg"/></a> <a href="https://git.rust-bitcoin.org/rust-bitcoin/rust-secp256k1/src/branch/master/LICENSE"><img alt="CC0 1.0 Universal Licensed" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-CC0--1.0-blue.svg"/></a> <a href="https://docs.rs/secp256k1-sys"><img alt="API Docs" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/docs.rs-secp256k1--sys-green"/></a> <a href="https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/08/11/Rust-1.63.0/"><img alt="Rustc Version 1.63.0+" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/rustc-1.63.0%2B-lightgrey.svg"/></a> </p> </div>

Provides low-level bindings to the C FFI exposed by libsecp256k1.

Vendoring

The default build process is to build using the vendored libsecp256k1 sources in the depend directory. These sources are prefixed with a special rust-secp256k1-sys-specific prefix rustsecp256k1_v0_14_.

This prefix ensures that no symbol collision can happen:

  • When a Rust project has two different versions of rust-secp256k1 in its depepdency tree, or
  • When rust-secp256k1 is used for building a static library in a context where existing libsecp256k1 symbols are already linked.

To update the vendored sources, use the vendor-libsecp.sh script: ./vendor-libsecp.sh <rev>

  • Where <rev> is the git revision of libsecp256k1 to checkout. You can even checkout PR branches by using <rev> as refs/pull/<PR-number>/head. If you do not specify a revision, the script will simply clone the repo and use whatever revision the default branch is pointing to.

Remember to update the *.patch files and ensure they apply cleanly. These files remove components that won't compile on WASM as they require stdlib methods. To do this:

  1. Checkout the content of each of the <file>.<extension>.patch files.
  2. On a clean version of libsecp256k1 checkout the <rev> you want to update.
git fetch <remote> <rev>
git checkout FETCH_HEAD
  1. For each <file>.<extension>.patch file, duplicate the content of <file>.<extension> on <file>.<extension>.modified:
cp <file>.<extension> <file>.<extension>.modified
  1. On <file>.<extension>.modified, remove each of the functions listed on the respective <file>.<extension>.patch files.
  2. Generate a new *.patch file for each of them with:
diff "<file>.<extension>" "<file>.<extension>.modified" > "<file>.<extension>.patch"
  1. Check the patches apply cleanly with:
patch --dry-run "<file>.<extension>" < "<file>.<extension>.patch"
  1. Replace the old *.patch files with the new generated ones in their expected paths.
  2. Now execute: ./vendor-libsecp.sh <rev>, on this repository.

Linking to external symbols

Danger: doing this incorrectly may have catastrophic consequences!

This is mainly intended for applications consisting of various programming languages that intend to link the same library to save space, or bundles of multiple binaries coming from the same source. Do not use this to link to a random secp256k1 library you found in your OS! If you are packaging software that depends on rust-secp256k1, using this flag to link to another package, make sure you stay within the binary compatibility guarantees of that package. For example, in Debian if you need libsecp256k1 1.2.3, make sure your package requires a version strictly>= 1.2.3 << 1.2.4. Note also that unless you're packaging the library for an official repository you should prefix your package and the library with a string specific to you. E.g. if you have a set of packages called my-awesome-packages you should package libsecp256k1 as libmy-awesome-packages-secp256k1 and depend on that library/package name from your application.

If you want to compile this library without using the bundled symbols (which may be required for integration into other build systems), you can do so by adding --cfg=rust_secp_no_symbol_renaming' to your RUSTFLAGS variable.

Minimum Supported Rust Version

This library should always compile with any combination of features on Rust 1.56.1.

CHANGELOG.md · Author-provided

0.14.1 - 2026-08-28

Metadata-only release; no code changes.

  • Point the crates.io repository/homepage metadata at https://git.rust-bitcoin.org/rust-bitcoin/rust-secp256k1 instead of GitHub.
  • Fix the LICENSE badge link in README.md to point at git.rust-bitcoin.org.

0.14.0 - 2026-08-27

  • Update libsecp256k1 to v0.8.0 #943
  • Add secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen_counter binding #941
  • Add secp256k1_tagged_sha256 binding #941
  • Drop SECP256K1_API from vendored symbols #930

0.13.0 - 2026-01-12

  • Update libsecp256k1 to v0.7.0.

0.12.0 - 2025-10-10

  • Fix lowmemory feature #799
  • Add support for MuSig2, initial PR #716 then a bunch of follow up PRs. See ../CHANGELOG.md for full listing.

0.10.0 - 2024-03-28

  • Bump MSRV to Rust v1.56.1 #693
  • Vendor secp256k1 v0.4.1 #688

0.9.2 - 2023-12-18

  • Fix incorrect FFI binding for secp256k1_pubkey_combine

0.9.1 - 2023-12-07

  • Patch out any instances of printf in upstream #663

0.9.0 - 2023-10-23

  • Add bindings to the ElligatorSwift implementation #627
  • Update vendored lib secp256k1 to v0.4.0 #653
  • Bump MSRV to 1.48 #595

0.8.1 - 2023-03-16

  • Implement insecure-erase.

0.8.0 - 2202-12-19

  • Update libsecp25k1 to v0.2.0

0.7.0 - 2022-12-01

  • Make comparison functions stable across library versions
  • Add public methods cmp_fast_unstable and eq_fast_unstable for types that contain an inner array (see PR linked above).

0.6.0 - 2022-06-21

  • Bump MSRV to 1.41
  • Re-implement Ord on PublicKey using upstream ordering function

0.5.1 - 2022-04-30

  • Fix WASM build

0.3.0 - 2020-08-27

  • Update MSRV to 1.29.0

0.2.0 - 2020-08-26

  • Update upstream to 670cdd3f8be25f81472b2d16dcd228b0d24a5c45
  • Add missing return c_int to NonceFn
  • Got wasm support working again
  • Removed cc restriction, rustc 1.22 support now requires some downstream effort
  • Exposed a reference to the underlying byte array for all byte-array-wrapping types
  • Allow all-zeroes Message to be constructed
  • Expose secp256k1_ec_pubkey_negate from upstream
